note: The fuzz target writes the raw PoC bytes to a temporary config file; config__read_file_core reads the line containing tls_engine_kpass_sha1 and a long all-zero hex string into buf.
The first space-delimited token is parsed from the attacker-controlled config line and becomes tls_engine_kpass_sha1.
The parsed directive selects the TLS engine SHA1 passphrase branch.
conf__parse_string duplicates the rest of the config line, so kpass_sha points to the PoC-controlled hex operand.
The unchecked hex string is passed to mosquitto__hex2bin_sha1 for conversion into a SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH-sized buffer.
The destination for conversion is a fixed 20-byte stack array because SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH is 20.
tmp and a maximum length of SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH are passed to mosquitto__hex2bin, but the callee writes leading zero bytes before enforcing that maximum.
The loop iterates over each leading 00 byte-pair in the PoC-controlled hex string.
Every byte-pair in the candidate value is 00, so the leading-zero path is repeatedly taken.
The 21st leading zero byte is written to bin[20], one byte past the 20-byte tmp stack buffer, before the later length check can reject it.
